messages.snippet: Hello folks!, How are you doing?, i hope well besides this crazy world, long time no see, most of you. I don't know whether this list is a bit death, since i haven't been following it much. I'm writing you to see the feelings about a bit di
messages.text:
Hello folks!,
How are you doing?, i hope well besides this crazy world, long time no see, most of you.
I don't know whether this list is a bit death, since i haven't been following it much. I'm writing you to see the feelings about a bit different boot...
In short: would any of you be interested on renting a boat for ~3 days from Malaga province (ES) and watch the total eclipse from the sea?
Background: some of you might know my "dream" on sailing in the warmer Mediterranean, though it won't be close to a hacker camp.
Since some months ago i live 15min walking to the Mediterranean in a ES big city, so i've being exploring sail boat rent options and even considering to get the PER [0] title that would allow me to sail until Balearic Islands from here.
As some of you already told me years ago, is more expensive here to rent a boat, about the double, which would mean ~100eur per person per day (not expensive compared with hostels price per night).
Regarding the eclipse, i've had the opportunity to watch the total eclipse of the 12 of August at only ~3.5h driving (usually would be 2.5h) without having to search for a place to sleep, so it feels worth it.
For the longer (in ES) next year eclipse, i'd need to sleep in site, since is farther away from my place, and as expected, it seems already very hard to find places to sleep (it's not allowed to freely camp, less in those dates with the big amount of tourists and fire risk).
Given all of that, i've thought that a possibility would be to sleep and watch the eclipse from a boat, and even see the reflection of the sun in the sea and have a darker sky.
On other next year events, i guess there'll be CCCamp, which i'd like to attend and maybe some of you were already thinking on boot near there.
Said all of this, i feel kind of crazy thinking on this given the world situation, and it isn't my only contradiction...
What do you think?
Cheers,
duy
PS: if the heat continues to be like this summer here, i might stop complaining about the cold sea in the usual boot spots...

messages.text:
View this post on the web at https://www.cremieux.xyz/p/how-do-you-ask-an-llm-a-question
Today’s post is brought to you by my sponsor, Mechanize [ https://substack.com/redirect/e6029ea0-3bd7-48dc-a7d3-9331d1f0d510?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ]. They’re hiring junior software engineers [ https://substack.com/redirect/4bfef94d-25a8-4c46-95cc-e8206c8df889?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] at $300K/year base salary.
The obvious answer to the headline question is that you would ask it a question in the same way you would ask a person, right? For some queries, I think that’s acceptable—(‘How big is the sun?’, ‘What’s 10+10?’, ‘Find a well-known mathematical conjecture and solve it. Make no mistakes.’)—, but often enough, it’s just not. In my experience, the key issues are obeisance, confidence, ‘nuance’, and tacit knowledge.
I’m going to consider three recent cases that I believe to be illustrative of these issues.
America’s High-Cost Healthcare
In 2014, Random Critical Analysis  (henceforth, “RCA”) produced an analysis [ https://substack.com/redirect/0e8c3211-898e-4df5-b9ce-2da9c8a67169?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] that decisively debunked a number of popular talking points about American spending, healthcare, and so on, and he popularized Actual Individual Consumption and its importance to the blogosphere and the Twitterati. This blogpost has produced an inordinate amount of ire because left-leaning (= center-left and further) and far-right people interested in politics often hold strong, non-empirical views and corresponding positions on the topic of American healthcare.
The main thing that RCA documented is that America is not a massive outlier in global healthcare spending once its vast wealth [ https://substack.com/redirect/218117ef-277f-4675-938f-ecdbb640bd6e?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] is accounted for. In other blogposts, he expanded on several potentially important points, debunking common ideas about the roles of inequality [ https://substack.com/redirect/d4be9d1a-744a-4858-92f3-4f7eeecef76b?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ], prices [ https://substack.com/redirect/86c94613-421f-4181-9c97-0c44a9ad7d8f?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] (see also [ https://substack.com/redirect/28c75566-d495-41b1-86fb-26a2c489955e?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmS

messages.text:
Executive Event Series Personal Invite
I wanted to personally invite you to an upcoming Legacy Lounge dinner on August 18 in San Francisco, hosted in partnership with Succedia Ventures. Funding Breakthrough Lab is a San Francisco-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit pre-accelerator built around a founder-first, rather than startup-first, philosophy. We believe exceptional founders should have greater access to the knowledge, networks, and resources that can meaningfully change the trajectory of what they build. That’s why we’ve partnered with Succedia Ventures to give our community access to a highly curated room of investors, capital allocators, experienced founders, and senior operators—people who can otherwise be difficult to meet in a meaningful setting for simple price of dinner ($59). AI has made it cheaper to build. It has also made it cheaper to copy. So before your next fundraise, product launch, or strategy meeting, every founder should be asking themselves these 5 questions: This dinner's topic: Defensible Moats AI has made it dramatically cheaper to build. It has also made it dramatically cheaper to copy. Which raises a harder question: What actually makes a company defensible when the technology itself becomes easier to replicate? Before your next fundraise, product launch, or strategy meeting, consider these five questions: The Moat Audit 1. If a competitor saw your roadmap tomorrow, what could they not reproduce? Features are rarely moats. Proprietary data, workflow ownership, distribution, regulatory access, IP, and trust can be. 2. What gets stronger every time a customer uses your product? If usage creates no compounding advantage, growth may be making you bigger—but not more defensible. 3. Are you embedded in a workflow, or simply sitting on top of it? The closer you are to mission-critical behavior, the harder you are to replace. 4. Does your business model capture the value your technology creates? Great technology paired with weak pricing or distribution can still create a weak company. 5. Which decision are you making today that will be painful to reverse in three years? Cap table. IP ownership. Governance. Partnerships. Data rights. Architecture. Defensibility is rarely one brilliant moat. It's a series of decisions that compound. On August 18, we're taking this conversation into the room. Four leaders from different disciplines will examine defensibility through their own lens, centered around one question: No decks. No founder pitch parade.

View this post on the web at https://www.californiacurrent.org/p/prop-4-your-money-their-campaigns
Proposition 4 Wants You to Pay for Politicians’ Campaigns
That’s the whole pitch, dressed up as “fair elections.”
Fair for whom, exactly?
For over five decades California has banned using public money to bankroll candidates. Voters put that rule in place for a very good reason: Nobody should be forced to fund the campaigns of the people who tax them.
Prop 4 would erase that ban.
That ban isn’t some dusty technicality. It came out of the Political Reform Act of 1974 and the sleaze around the CREEP payments during Watergate. The principle was simple: your tax dollars are for roads, schools, cops, and hospitals—not for paying consultants to tell you how wonderful their candidate is or how terrible his opponent looks.
Or to fund dirty political tricks.
Think about what Prop 4 means in practice. A small-business owner already struggling with high taxes and fees would now be required to help bankroll the very politician who just voted to raise them again. A parent frustrated with failing schools, such as I, would be forced to subsidize the campaign of a CTA-sponsored board member running to keep the status quo intact.
You don’t get a refund if you hate the candidate’s platform. Taxpayers on the Right will be forced to fund Leftist politicians. Taxpayers on the Left will be forced to fund Right wing politicians. You don’t get to check a box that says, “Not with my money.”
The state simply takes it and hands it over.
What’s worse is that the funding amounts, administration, and details are not even spelled out. Should it pass, the state and local governments would set up those undefined rules later. Those rules will be written, of course, by those already in charge of the place.
Prop 4 is Literally a Blank Check
Supporters say this levels the playing field. It doesn’t. It does, however, coerce you into picking up the tab for what may well be your least favorite politician.
Incumbents still get the money. Challengers still need to qualify. And every taxpayer—left, right, or checked out—ends up bankrolling attack ads and mailers for candidates they may actively despise. You don’t get to opt out. That’s not democracy.
Passage of Prop 4 would be compulsory speech enforced by taxation.

24.7 — River and canal ships generated  [ https://substack.com/redirect/d310e20d-7524-4faa-93b7-a682226114a7?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ]24.7% [ https://substack.com/redirect/d310e20d-7524-4faa-93b7-a682226114a7?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] of global shipping CO2 emissions in 2022, despite these waterways making up less than 1% of the world’s navigable water.
22— The Dallas Cowboys are now worth  [ https://substack.com/redirect/9d40f597-0679-4c60-b27d-c306104ce4ef?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ]$15.5 billion, a 22% [ https://substack.com/redirect/63306f57-cc44-4431-b2d8-9c180f550a5a?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] jump over 2025 that makes them the most valuable franchise in American sports.
Believing Is Seeing
Your brain runs into walls it never saw coming, literally. Neuroscientists have found that the brain doesn’t passively receive sensory data and react, it constantly makes top-down predictions about what should be there, and only flags a problem when reality contradicts the guess, a mismatch researchers call a “prediction error.” This is why you might wave at a stranger you mistook for a friend, or swear the keys aren’t on the table when they’re sitting right in front of you, your mind fills gaps and edits out surprises to keep the picture coherent. Even your deepest beliefs, shaped by an evolutionary craving for safety and stability, work the same way, acting as filters that decide what counts as true before you ever really look. The unsettling upshot is that you don’t see, then believe, you believe, then see, and getting better at decisions starts with catching your brain’s bets before they go wrong. Bioneer,
The Lorax once asked, "Who will speak for the trees?" Today, trees — and the seas, the soil, the waterways, the animals facing extinction — need more than people speaking for them. They need people willing to write laws for them, and go to court for them.
Indigenous communities have long understood what our legal systems are only beginning to confront: Our laws are failing to protect people and planet. All over the world, people are fighting to protect what remains of the natural world. But too often, the law doesn't recognize ecosystems, rivers, or species as having a right to survive.
This course explores the growing movement to Indigenize the law — bringing Traditional Ecological Knowledge and Indigenous principles of reciprocity into the black letter of the law, so we can, in fact, sue for the trees.
“We are not protecting nature. We are nature protecting itself.”
— Casey Camp Horinek
Join us to hear directly from leaders in the Rights of Nature and Earth Law movements: people who are crafting, passing, and implementing new laws built on old principles.
Bioneers has supported the Rights of Nature movement since Ecuador became the first country to recognize it in 2008, working alongside Indigenous youth from the Mashpee Wampanoag to Kanaka Maoli. This course continues that work.
This is not just a course. It is a call to action.

Evan here — with an exciting update to share.
We're launching** The Climatebase Scholarship Fund** — and we're thrilled to announce **[Climatize](https://climatize.earth/climatebase)**** as its first partner, sponsoring 10 dedicated scholarships for cohort 10 of the **[**Climatebase Fellowship**](https://climatebase.org/fellowship?utm_source=stories.climatebase.org&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=announcing-the-climatebase-scholarship-fund-with-climatize-as-our-first-partner)**.**
Our partnership with Climatize isn't new:
* **Climatebase members have collectively **[**funded $150,000**](https://climatize.earth/climatebase)** of real decarbonization projects** **through Climatize** — including community solar in Maryland where 51% of the power benefits low-income communities, battery storage in Texas, and EV charging at multi-family housing in California. Real impact.
* **Climatize has hired multiple multiple Climatebase Fellows** — including their recently promoted Director of Engineering — directly from past Fellowship cohorts.
* **Fellowship graduate Stephan Ng recently used Climatize to raise $424,000 for his startup, **[**Moonfive**](https://web.climatize.earth/project/00053)**. **
Real impact. In both directions.
The Climatebase Scholarship Fund builds upon our ongoing commitment to ensuring the Climatebase Fellowship is accessible to qualified applicants. Over the past five years, the we’ve awarded **more than $1 million in financial aid** to applicants to participate in the Fellowship.
**To be considered for one of the ten Climatize-sponsored scholarships, make sure you **[**apply**](https://climatebase.org/fellowship?utm_source=stories.climatebase.org&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=announcing-the-climatebase-scholarship-fund-with-climatize-as-our-first-partner)** by the final Cohort 10 application deadline: August 24.**

The country’s top lawyer is now a “thank you very much, I love you sir [ https://substack.com/redirect/a84b1cef-85e1-41ae-9c42-1987798900ce?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ]” yes-man. He has the job purely out of willingness to protect Donald Trump and prosecute his enemies. Republicans in the Senate knew this and confirmed him anyway. Norms, laws, consequences, the Constitution — all of them be damned. At least Pam Bondi seemed a little bit uncomfortable acting as the president’s chief enforcer.
And yet… I just can’t get myself that worked up over him.
“Is this,” I asked myself, “the inevitable frog-in-boiling-water desensitization [ https://substack.com/redirect/7ab484e0-fc1e-428c-83c8-68d258d0cd87?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] that authoritarianism brings?”

Yes, Todd Blanche is Donald Trump’s dream attorney general. He’s a ruthless political operator who will gleefully wield the powers of federal law enforcement against both political opponents and the electoral process.

Every serious reporter, litigator, judge, elections official, state or local prosecutor, commentator, and politics-watcher understands that Blanche sees himself [ https://substack.com/redirect/9da133dc-f950-4cbd-820f-8cb592960b4e?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] as a presidential consigliere. View this post on the web at https://www.founderfridays.co/p/founder-fridays-no-207
Happy Friday.
Did a savvy founder forward this to you? Subscribe below for weekly insights that help you scale smarter.
An Enduring Company on One Product
Charles Brannock built a company in 1925, refused to ever expand beyond his single foot-measuring device, never took venture money, and it’s still profitable a hundred years later — while Payless, backed by private equity and “modernized” with debt, went bankrupt and disappeared. The lesson isn’t nostalgia, it’s that relentless focus on making one thing well, funded by real revenue instead of leverage, builds something that survives market shifts and cheap knockoffs because customers can feel the difference in quality. This week, pick the one part of your product you’d stake your reputation on, and go find where you’ve quietly let quality slip to hit a growth number — a Brannock exec once won a huge account just by showing the buyer a broken competitor’s part next to his own. Do that consistently and you get what most “hot” startups never do: a business that doesn’t need the next funding round or acquisition to survive the next decade. 99% Invisible [ https://substack.com/redirect/263d70bb-5fc4-4d3d-9427-6eac181264eb?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] (18 minutes)
Fix Your Board Slides
Here’s the uncomfortable truth: giving equal weight to all your quarterly goals doesn’t show discipline — it’s a confession that you don’t know how to prioritize, and it’s often how founders accidentally lie to themselves about how much trouble they’re in. A founder with four months of runway who lists “fundraising” and “ship feature X” as equal-sized boxes on a slide isn’t being balanced, they’re avoiding the one number that should be dominating every decision they make. So this week, rebuild your next board slide with sized boxes, not a bulleted list — runway under 12 months means fundraising takes up 95% of the slide in giant font, full stop, and every other goal shrinks to match its actual urgency. Do this and your board meeting stops being theater where you perform “fine” — it becomes the one recurring moment that forces you to check your plan against reality before a shrinking runway turns into a crisis nobody saw coming.
